title: Woman Raising Hand Emoji 🙋‍♀️ Meaning: “Pick Me!” and Hello
description: 🙋‍♀️ means “me!”, “I volunteer,” “I have a question” or a cheerful hi. See how the woman raising hand emoji is used in group chats, polls and captions.
summary: 🙋‍♀️ shows a smiling woman with one arm raised straight up. It works like raising your hand in class: “me!”, “I’ll do it,” “guilty” or “question.” Many people also send it as a bright hello. Women often pick this version to put themselves in the picture when they volunteer or agree.
meaning: The gesture is about as literal as emoji get. A hand in the air asks to be counted, and 🙋‍♀️ is how many women answer “who’s in?” in a group chat, claim the last slice of cake, or own up to something: “who forgot to buy ice? 🙋‍♀️.” It is one of the few gestures that signals pure eagerness, which gives it a cheerful, slightly goofy energy.

Its official Unicode name is Happy Person Raising One Hand, and most platforms draw the face smiling. That cheerfulness is why it doubles as a greeting. A single 🙋‍♀️ at the start of a message reads as “hi, it’s me!”, and some people use it to announce they have arrived in a chat, a livestream comment section or a new online community.

It also handles confessions with good humor. When someone asks who is guilty of a relatable habit, like keeping dozens of browser tabs open or eating cereal for dinner, replying 🙋‍♀️ admits it without shame. The raised hand turns an admission into a joke shared with everyone else who does the same thing, and captions and memes use it this way all the time.

The woman variant arrived in 2016 alongside a man version. Before that, some platforms already drew the plain 🙋 as a woman, so some users simply kept the look they knew. Today it works largely as a self-representation: women use it when the raised hand is theirs, and others use it when describing a specific woman who jumped at a chance.

contexts.label: In group chats and polls
contexts.body: This is its natural habitat. Planning a dinner, a carpool or a group gift, people reply 🙋‍♀️ to sign up without typing a full sentence. It is quick, unambiguous and friendly. When a whole column of raised hands appears under a question, organizers can practically count heads from the emojis alone and move on.

contexts.label: In captions and comments
contexts.body: On Instagram and TikTok, “who else does this? 🙋‍♀️” invites viewers to identify with a habit, and commenters answer with raised hands of their own. Creators use it in Q&A posts to mean “ask me anything” or to introduce a round of answers. It signals approachability and a willingness to join in.

contexts.label: In class and study groups
contexts.body: Students use it literally in chat-based lessons and study servers to signal a question without interrupting whoever is speaking. It carries classroom manners into text well. It is clearer than typing a lone question mark, because it shows who is asking and that they are politely waiting for their turn.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Volunteering in a team channel with 🙋‍♀️ is generally welcome and reads as keen: “I can take the Friday shift 🙋‍♀️.” It also works for quick questions in meetings run over chat. It is informal, though, so in messages to senior leaders or clients a short written answer looks more polished.

examples.text: Me! 🙋‍♀️ I’ll take the extra ticket
examples.meaning: Eagerly claiming something on offer before anyone else can.

examples.text: Guilty 🙋‍♀️ I still have Christmas lights up in March
examples.meaning: Owning up to a relatable habit with good humor.
Politely signaling she wants to ask something before asking it.
A cheerful hello announcing that she has arrived.
Volunteering for a task while the group is making plans.

examples.text: Who else cries at every dog movie? 🙋‍♀️
examples.meaning: Inviting others to admit the same soft spot she has.

combos.meaning: Enthusiastic volunteering: yes, me, and I am excited about it.
Sheepishly admitting she is the one responsible for a small mess.
A doubled greeting, extra friendly and bouncy.
She has a question and is waiting for her turn to ask it.

confusedWith.difference: 🙋 is the gender-neutral base, with the same “me!” and hello meanings. 🙋‍♀️ shows a woman specifically, so it is chosen when the sender wants the raised hand to look like her or is describing a particular woman.
✋ is a bare hand with the palm out, used for “stop,” a high five or “hold on.” 🙋‍♀️ includes the person and her smile, so it means volunteering or greeting rather than halting someone.
💁‍♀️ holds the palm low near her shoulder and reads as sassy or informative. 🙋‍♀️ reaches up high to be noticed. The two sit side by side on most keyboards and are often mixed up by accident.

avoid: Do not use it to volunteer for something you are not sure you can deliver, since it reads as a firm yes.
Avoid it as a greeting in formal emails, where a written hello fits better.
design: One arm goes straight up above her head, palm facing forward, like a student who knows the answer. Most designs pair the raised hand with a bright, open smile, in line with the happy figure named in the official character name. Hair and clothing vary by platform, and the emoji supports the full range of skin tones.

faqs.q: What does 🙋‍♀️ mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Most likely she is volunteering, agreeing or admitting something: “me too,” “I’ll do it” or “guilty.” As an opener, it is a friendly hello. It is upbeat and open, and it carries no hidden romantic meaning on its own.

Often, yes. Because the woman is smiling with her hand up, many people send it as a greeting or to announce they have joined a chat. The waving hand 👋 is the more standard hello, but 🙋‍♀️ feels warmer and more animated.
Treat it like a raised hand in a room. If she is volunteering, confirm or assign the task. If she has a question, invite her to ask. If it is a hello, greet her back. In a poll, count it as a yes.

faqs.q: Is there a man version of this emoji?
faqs.a: Yes. 🙋‍♂️ shows a man raising his hand, and the neutral 🙋 shows a person without a specified gender. All three were available by 2016, and they share the same meanings of volunteering, agreeing and greeting.
